opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ann Patrick (employee ID E035) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E035.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Ann Patrick (E035) is a full-time Engineer. As an Engineer, she owns the Source Code system, so admin access is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E035 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note lists full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractors can only have read without advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: E035 (Ann Patrick) requested admin access to Source Code. The Security agent's database (authoritative for employment type) shows E035 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E035 requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory has two notes:

Note 1 (HR agent):
- role: Engineer
- employment type: full_time
- recommendation: admin
- Comment: full-time Engineer owns Source Code, so admin permitted.

Note 2 (Security agent):
- role: Engineer (not looked up in own database; same as HR)
- employment type: contractor (looked up in own database)
- security training: basic
- recommendation: read
- Comment: Security DB shows contractor; Security DB authoritative for employment type. Contractors can only have read without advanced training, never admin.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security says their DB is authoritative for employment type.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If employee is full-time Engineer (owns Source Code), admin is permitted → grant admin (requested level).
If employee is contractor with basic training, max is read → grant read.

Which to believe? The Security agent claims Security DB is authoritative for employment type. The HR agent looked up own database for employment type. There's a conflict. We need to decide.

The instructions say use available information. Security note says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. So employment type = contractor. Role = Engineer (both agree). Security training = basic (from Security).

Contractor: max read (no advanced training), never admin. Requested admin exceeds max → grant read.

Also note: role Engineer owns Source Code, but for contractors admin is never allowed regardless of ownership.

So decision: read.

Let me submit read.
